scale_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare draft company-level OKRs for the upcoming quarter, to be tracked in Notion and/or Linear. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our company mission/strategy notes or last quarter's OKRs (documents, Notion pages, or Linear projects), (2) our current quarter's business priorities or board/leadership updates, (3) which tool (Notion, Linear, or both) should host the OKRs, and (4) how many objectives I want drafted (typically 3-5) with 2-4 key results each.

Using this input, please:
1. Review prior OKRs (if available) and note which were achieved, missed, or carried over.
2. Draft 3-5 candidate company-level Objectives that are ambitious, qualitative, and time-bound to the quarter, each with 2-4 measurable Key Results (specific numbers, dates, or thresholds).
3. For each draft objective, briefly note the rationale (why it matters now) and any dependency or risk you noticed in the source material.
4. Create a new Notion page or Linear project/document titled clearly (e.g., "Q_ 20__ Company OKRs - DRAFT") containing these candidates in a clean, reviewable format, but do not mark them final or share them broadly.
5. Prepare a short summary (objectives + key results + rationale) suitable for a leadership review meeting.

Do not finalize, publish, or announce these objectives — setting company objectives is a strategic leadership decision. Once the draft document and summary are ready, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the link/location of the draft document, a summary of each proposed objective and its key results, and any open questions or gaps in data you found while drafting.

scale_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up a quarterly OKR tracking system in {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization details and confirmation you can access it with configured credentials, (2) the current quarter/year to use as the initial tracking period, (3) the list of company-level objectives (if I have them drafted) or confirm you should create placeholder structure for me to fill in, and (4) the names of teams whose objectives should be tracked separately.

Once you have this, prepare (but do NOT create yet) a plan for an OKR database/workspace structure in {{vendor}} that includes:
- A database or page structure for Objectives, each with fields for: level (Company/Team/Individual), owning team, status, priority, and quarter.
- Linked Key Results under each Objective, with fields for progress/metric tracking.
- A shared docs/notes area alongside the OKR database for context, updates, and retros, organized so it sits next to the tracked objectives.
- Views or filters grouping objectives by team, level, and status for easy review.

Draft the exact database schema (property names, types, and options) and page layout as a written spec, plus sample entries for one company objective and one team objective, so I can review before anything is built.

Do not create, modify, or publish anything in {{vendor}} yet — this requires my explicit approval. Present the full draft plan and schema to me for review, then stop for human sign-off.

When reporting back, give me: the proposed database structure, sample entries, any open questions (e.g., naming conventions, permissions, quarter naming), and a short checklist of what you will create once I approve.

scale_012:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare draft Team OKRs for this quarter's OKR cycle, tracked in Notion or Linear (whichever we use — ask me if unclear). Team OKR entries must align to our approved Company OKRs.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have:
1. The current quarter's Company Objectives and Key Results (paste text or a link/page reference).
2. Which tool we track OKRs in (Notion or Linear) and where (workspace/database or project name).
3. The list of teams that need Team OKRs this quarter, and for each team, the team lead's name and any context on capacity, recent priorities, or constraints.

Then, for each team:
- Draft 2–4 Team Objectives that plausibly ladder up to one or more Company Objectives, each with 2–4 measurable Key Results.
- Clearly label each draft as "DRAFT — pending team lead approval" and note which Company Objective it supports.
- Create these as entries/pages/issues in the specified tool, using our existing OKR template or structure if one exists (ask me if you're unsure of the format), but do not mark them as final, active, or approved.

Do not commit the team to specific targets, do not mark any OKR as approved or active, and do not notify anyone that these are final. Each team lead must review, adjust based on their own judgment of what's realistically achievable, and explicitly approve before these become official — this remains a human step for their sign-off.

When done, report back: the tool/location where drafts were created, a summary of each team's draft Objectives and Key Results with their linked Company Objective, and confirm you have stopped and are awaiting each team lead's review — stop for human sign-off before any Team OKR is finalized or activated.

scale_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up quarterly OKR tracking in {{vendor}} by preparing new projects for each Key Result, one project per KR, ready for my review before anything is created.

Before starting, ask me for anything missing: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/domain and confirmation you can use my configured credentials, (2) the current quarter's Objectives and their Key Results (text list), (3) which team should own each KR project, (4) the priority level to assign to each (e.g., high/medium/low), (5) the initial status each project should start in (e.g., planned/backlog), and (6) whether an existing project template should be used as the starting point for these KR projects.

Once you have this, draft, for each Key Result, a project spec including: project name (tie it clearly to the parent Objective and KR), owning team, priority, initial status, and a short description restating the KR's target metric and due date (end of quarter unless I say otherwise). If a template exists, note which template each draft would be built from.

Compile all drafted project specs into a single clear summary list (one per KR) for my review. Do not create, submit, or apply any of these projects in {{vendor}} yet — only prepare the drafts and present them to me.

When the drafts are ready, stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full list of proposed KR projects (name, team, priority, status, description, template used if any) and explicitly state you are waiting for my approval before any project is created in {{vendor}}.

scale_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me kick off our quarterly OKR framework by sending an announcement to the team in {{vendor}}, our team-chat tool. Goal: draft and prepare (but NOT send) a kickoff message that announces the new OKR process, explains that company, team, and individual objectives will be tracked in Linear/Notion, and invites the team to a kickoff meeting or async review.

Before drafting, ask me for: (1) the target {{vendor}} channel or room name (create one if needed, e.g. a 'company-okrs' channel), (2) the quarter/timeframe for this OKR cycle, (3) links to the Linear/Notion OKR tracker, (4) the kickoff date/deadline for individual objectives, and (5) any key company-level objectives already defined that should be highlighted.

Once you have these, draft the kickoff message content (clear, concise, includes purpose, timeline, tracker links, and next steps for each team). Also prepare the exact mechanism to send it — using your configured credentials, determine whether {{vendor}} supports posting via its API, an incoming webhook, or a CLI send command, and prepare the fully filled-in request or command (channel/target, message text) ready to execute, but do not send or post it yet.

Produce a short checklist showing: target channel, message draft, and the prepared send action (API call, webhook payload, or CLI command) ready to trigger.

Done looks like: a complete draft message, a confirmed destination channel, and a ready-to-run send action, all presented to me for review. Because sending requires my explicit approval before it goes live, do not post the message — stop for human sign-off and wait for my confirmation before executing the send.
